correctness.rationale: Let Z omit the two incompatible central arrows. It is the join C_a*C_b of connected crown graphs; reduced H3(Z)=A_a⊠A_b as an integral G-module, other reduced groups vanish. The two central-arrow stars are cones on opposite-oriented links L_+,L_- each exactly K_{a,b}, and are never simultaneously present, yielding the equivariant relative chain decomposition and H2(X,Z)=H1(K_ab)^2. The H1(K_ab) lattice consists of zero-row/zero-column-sum integer matrices and is exactly V_a⊗V_b, integrally. The LES gives canonical degree-separated H3(X)=H3(Z), H2(X)=H2(X,Z), no hidden extension/splitting problem. For leaf permutations trace on V_t is f−1 and on crown H1 is p(f) from oriented edge/vertex counts. If hubs interchange, the two cone contributions exchange and have zero trace in degree2; swapping the two degree-one homology factors in the join has Koszul sign (−1)^{(1+1)(1+1)}=+1, so χ3=p(f(στ)). Independently enumerated all 201 augmented faces for a=b=3, got reduced mod2 Betti (β2,β3)=(8,1), and directly computed signed Lefschetz traces for five identity/transposition/hub-swap elements; all matched formula. Reviewed the 3,885-byte source verifier, which tests full small group actions. Universal proof is relative integral topology, not a finite experiment.
residual_risks: For a=b the swapping action on degree three requires the correct join-interchange orientation sign; explicitly verified as +1 for pairs of one-cycles.
